summary: The Chinese Government Scholarship - Silk Road Program is a sub-programme that the Ministry of Education has run since 2017 to bring young students from Belt and Road partner countries to degree study at selected Chinese universities. Each participating university recruits its own candidates, sets its own eligible countries, programmes, language rules and dates, and then nominates candidates to the China Scholarship Council, which makes the final decision. Benefits described by the universities are a tuition waiver, accommodation, a monthly allowance and comprehensive medical insurance. The 2026 notices have closed; this file records what the universities published for the 2026 and 2026-2027 round.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants must be non-Chinese citizens of a country that the host university lists for its Silk Road places. The lists differ by university. Examples for 2026: Tianjin University lists Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Cambodia, Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh, Russia, Nigeria and Morocco; Nankai University lists Vietnam, Malaysia, Thailand, Myanmar, Pakistan, Mongolia, Indonesia, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and Colombia; China Pharmaceutical University lists Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, Mongolia, Tanzania, Egypt, Russia and Uzbekistan; Central South University lists Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nigeria, Yemen, Ethiopia, Afghanistan, Indonesia, Turkmenistan, Tanzania and Russia; Shaanxi Normal University lists Russia, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Indonesia, Malaysia, Pakistan, Thailand, Ethiopia, Ghana and Egypt; Beijing Foreign Studies University lists New Zealand, Portugal, Costa Rica, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Russia.

Level and age (Tianjin, Nankai, China Pharmaceutical University, Central South University): bachelor's applicants hold a high school diploma and are under 25; master's applicants hold a bachelor's degree and are under 35; PhD applicants hold a master's degree and are under 40. Applicants under 18 need guardianship documents notarised in China (Tianjin, BFSU, Changsha University of Science and Technology).

General conditions: good moral character, good physical and mental health, no criminal record, willingness to follow Chinese law and university rules. Applicants must not hold other Chinese government or university scholarships; Central South University and Shaanxi Normal University require a signed statement and bar applicants who hide other funding for three years.

Language (examples): Chinese-taught programmes need HSK, with minimum levels and scores set by each university (Tianjin HSK 5 at 180; Nankai HSK 5 at 210; China Pharmaceutical University HSK 4 at 220; Central South University HSK 4 at 260, or 180 to 259 with one preparatory year; BFSU HSK 4 at 180 exempts from the CSCA Chinese test). English-taught programmes need TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo (Tianjin TOEFL 80 or IELTS 6.0; Nankai IELTS 6.0, TOEFL 80 or Duolingo 105; China Pharmaceutical University TOEFL 90 or IELTS 6.5; Central South University IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL 85; Shaanxi Normal IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL 80). Native speakers or those taught in the language are generally exempt after the university certifies it.

Undergraduate applicants must submit a CSCA score report (subjects vary by university; Huazhong University of Science and Technology asks for Professional Chinese, Mathematics and Physics, carried over from stored data).

The 2026 notices also say that applicants who have emigrated or have a Chinese parent need proof of naturalisation and renunciation of Chinese nationality (Tianjin).
age_experience_notes: Bachelor's under 25, master's under 35, PhD under 40 at the universities read. Huazhong University of Science and Technology requires age under 25 and birth after 1 September 2001 for its 2026 bachelor's places (carried over from stored data). No work experience is required in the notices read.
funding_summary: Described by the universities, not by a single national page. Typical items: tuition waiver, on-campus accommodation, a monthly living allowance of CNY 2,500 (bachelor's), CNY 3,000 (master's) and CNY 3,500 (PhD), and comprehensive medical insurance. Variations: Beijing Foreign Studies University gives free housing or a CNY 700 monthly subsidy if the student rents, and says applicants pay their own travel; Huazhong University of Science and Technology states medical insurance of CNY 800 a year (carried over from stored data). Funding length follows the programme; Tianjin lists scholarship durations of 5 years (bachelor's, Chinese-taught), 2.5 to 4 years (master's, Chinese-taught), 2 to 3 years (master's, English-taught) and 3 to 5 years (PhD), which include a preparatory Chinese year where needed. Stipends and conditions are renewed through an annual review (Central South University).
programmes_note: Fields and levels depend entirely on the host university. Programmes named in the 2026 notices: bachelor's - Software Engineering and Architecture (Huazhong University of Science and Technology, carried over from stored data), Business Economics, Business Administration and Finance (Nankai), Chinese Language and Literature with a Chinese and other languages translation direction (BFSU), New Energy Science and Engineering (Changsha University of Science and Technology); master's - International Business and International Affairs and Public Policy (Nankai), Power Engineering and Engineering Thermophysics (Changsha University of Science and Technology), and five fields at Central South University; doctoral - five fields at Central South University and five English-taught fields at Shaanxi Normal University. Tianjin University and China Pharmaceutical University show their major catalogues only as images. Programme lists are subject to China Scholarship Council approval.
institutions_note: Participating universities each have an agency number for the China Scholarship Council system and use Program Category Type B. Read this round: Tianjin University (10056), Nankai University (10055), China Pharmaceutical University (10316), Central South University (10533), Beijing Foreign Studies University (10030), Shaanxi Normal University (10718), Changsha University of Science and Technology (10536) and Huazhong University of Science and Technology (carried over from stored data). Other universities also take part; no complete official list was found.

benefits.conditions: Beijing Foreign Studies University: free university housing, or a CNY 700 monthly subsidy if the student rents. On-campus housing depends on availability at some universities.

benefits.limit_text: CNY 2,500 per month (bachelor's), CNY 3,000 per month (master's), CNY 3,500 per month (PhD)
benefits.conditions: Stated by Tianjin, Nankai (bachelor's and master's), China Pharmaceutical University, Central South University (master's and PhD), Shaanxi Normal University (PhD) and BFSU (bachelor's).
Huazhong University of Science and Technology states CNY 800 a year (carried over from stored data).

benefits.conditions: Other universities read do not mention a travel allowance.

requirements.text: Passport copy valid beyond the date the university states (universities read: valid beyond September 2026, until at least 1 September 2027, or until September 2028 depending on the university); visa page if you are already in China.

Diploma scans for high school, bachelor's and master's as relevant. If the degree is not yet awarded by the deadline, a pre-graduation certificate; the notarised highest diploma is needed before registration.
Notarised transcripts of high school, bachelor's and master's study as relevant, covering every semester; current students submit transcripts to date and the full set before registration.
HSK for Chinese-taught programmes; TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo (or proof of English-medium study) for English-taught programmes, at the score the university sets.
CSCA score report (subjects set by the university).
Study experience resume with continuous dates starting from senior middle school (Tianjin, China Pharmaceutical University).

Study or research plan in English or Chinese: bachelor's at least 600 words, master's at least 800 words (China Pharmaceutical University) or 1,000 words (Tianjin), PhD at least 1,000 words; Nankai master's personal statement at least 800 words.
Provisional acceptance letter or form from a professor at the university (compulsory at China Pharmaceutical University and Central South University for master's and PhD; optional at Tianjin).
Two recommendation letters from professors or associate professors (master's and PhD); one for bachelor's at Nankai. In Chinese or English.

application_steps.title: Find a university that offers Silk Road places for your country
application_steps.detail: Each participating university publishes its own notice with eligible countries, levels, programmes and dates. Check that your citizenship is on the list and that you meet the age, degree and language rules for the level you want.

application_steps.title: Apply in the university's online application system
application_steps.detail: Upload the document list required by the university. Fees differ: the Nankai, Tianjin and BFSU notices mention no fee, Central South University and Changsha University of Science and Technology charge CNY 500 (Central South only after primary review), and Huazhong University of Science and Technology charges CNY 600 or USD 100 (carried over from stored data). Deadlines in 2026 fell between mid-May and 1 June at the universities read.

application_steps.title: Apply in the CSC system once nominated
application_steps.detail: After the university nominates you and issues a pre-admission letter, log in to the Chinese Government Scholarship information system, choose Program Type B and enter the university's agency number. Some universities (Central South University, Shaanxi Normal University, BFSU) require both systems from the start. Do not apply to both CSC and a university scholarship programme at the same time (Central South University).

application_steps.title: University review, interview and exams
application_steps.detail: The university reviews documents, then may hold an interview or written exam (Tianjin: May to July 2026; China Pharmaceutical University interviews 18 to 20 May 2026; Central South University: primary review, academic review, final review). Missing the interview counts as withdrawal. No scoring weights are published.

application_steps.title: CSC final decision
application_steps.detail: The university forwards the nominated candidates to the China Scholarship Council, which makes the final admission decision and notifies the university; timing is set by the Council each year. Results and admission notices were sent from 1 to 31 July 2026 at Tianjin and by 31 July at China Pharmaceutical University. Students recommended by Central South University may not receive a government scholarship; the admission notice states the final type.

application_steps.title: Receive the admission notice and visa form
application_steps.detail: Winners receive the admission notice and visa application form (JW201 or JW202), apply for a study visa and register at the end of August or early September. Missing registration or failing the enrolment medical check cancels the award (BFSU, Central South University).

application_steps.title: Keep the award through annual review
application_steps.detail: Scholarships are renewed through an annual review of academic and daily performance; failure leads to suspension or cancellation. Scholars cannot change university, major or study period, and may not hold other Chinese government or university scholarships (Central South University, BFSU, Shaanxi Normal University).
